name: honcho
description: Memory that reasons. Honcho builds a continually updated model of the people and agents you work with and answers questions about them, across every app and agent connected to it.

interface.longDescription:
Honcho gives ChatGPT a memory that reasons. Instead of a flat log of past messages, Honcho builds a continually updated model of the people and agents in your conversations, then answers questions about them in plain language.

The same memory follows you everywhere Honcho is connected: ChatGPT, Codex, dots, Claude, Cursor, and your own apps built on the Honcho SDK. What one agent learns, the next one already knows.

What you can do:
- Ask what Honcho knows: "what do I care about when reviewing code?" Honcho reasons over everything it has observed and answers directly.
- Search across past conversations, scoped to a person, a session, or a whole workspace.
- Read the facts Honcho has drawn about you, and see what each one was built from.
- Tell it to remember something specific, and it is there in your next conversation and every other connected app.
- Model more than one person: teams and multi-person conversations each get their own representation.

Honcho is open source (github.com/plastic-labs/honcho) and available as a managed service at app.honcho.dev. You need a free Honcho account to connect.
defaultPrompt: What does Honcho know about me?
Catch me up on what I've been working on lately.
Remember that I prefer short, direct answers.

positive.description: Recall how one person prefers to learn, reasoned over a long conversation history.
positive.prompt: Using Honcho, how does maya prefer to learn new material?
positive.expected_behavior: Answers that maya learns from examples and full sentences before rules, and disengages from repetitive drilling.

positive.description: Reason across two people in a shared, multi-person conversation.
positive.prompt: Using Honcho, what are maya and sam planning together, and where do their preferences differ?
positive.expected_behavior: Describes a two-week trip to Japan; maya wants structure, sam wants unscheduled time.

positive.description: Search past conversations for a specific topic.
positive.prompt: Search Honcho for what was said about counters in Japanese.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns messages from the japanese-tutoring session where maya works on Japanese counters.

positive.description: Show the stored profile Honcho keeps for a person.
positive.prompt: Show me Honcho's peer card for maya.
positive.expected_behavior: Lists biographical facts about maya, including that she studies Japanese in the early mornings before work and is planning a two-week spring trip to Japan with sam.

positive.description: Save one fact the user explicitly asks Honcho to remember.
positive.prompt: Remember in Honcho that sam prefers window seats on long flights.
positive.expected_behavior: Creates one conclusion about sam stating the seat preference, and confirms it was saved. Nothing else from the conversation is stored.

negative.prompt: What's the weather in Tokyo today?
negative.expected_behavior: Does not call Honcho; the request has nothing to do with stored memory.

negative.description: General coding task unrelated to memory.
negative.prompt: Write a Python function that reverses a string.
negative.expected_behavior: Does not call Honcho; answers the coding question directly.

negative.description: Sensitive personal data Honcho does not hold.
negative.prompt: Use Honcho to find maya's passport number and home address.
negative.expected_behavior: Does not invent the data. Honcho holds no such facts, so the answer says it is not available.
